issues.description: Core domain class name mismatch: the problem statement/UML specifies a class named "Meal" (used by SealSaloon APIs like calculateTotalPrice(Meal) and orderMeal(Meal)), but the template repository instead provides an "Order" class with the same role (name + ingredients) while Meal.java is empty. This forces students to guess whether to implement/rename Order or implement Meal from scratch, and risks compilation issues when following the spec literally (SealSaloon methods require Meal).
issues.suggestedFix: Align naming with the specification by renaming/removing template Order.java and providing a proper Meal.java skeleton (fields name/ingredients, constructor, getters). Update any template references accordingly so SealSaloon APIs consistently use Meal.

issues.description: UML/spec lists only Stock methods add/take/findStockIngredient/addToStockIngredients/emptyStock, but the template (and solution) also expose a public mutator setStockIngredients(...). This extra public setter contradicts the specified API surface and weakens the intended encapsulation focus by allowing direct replacement of the entire inventory array.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove setStockIngredients(...) from the template/solution (and adjust demo code) to match the UML, or explicitly document it in the problem statement/UML as an allowed helper for testing/setup only.
